name: Pass Thurn
kurzbeschreibung: Pass Thurn at 1,274 metres elevation links Kitzbühel with the Salzburg Pinzgau region, boasting protected moorland reserves and magnificent High Tauern panoramas.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Pass Thurn, sitting at an elevation of 1,274 metres, represents one of Austria's most historic and scenic mountain passes, forming the natural border and road link between Kitzbühel in Tirol and Mittersill in the Salzburg Pinzgau. Nestled in the heart of the Kitzbühel Alps, this gentle mountain saddle bridges the rounded slate peaks of the local range with the glaciated giants of the Hohe Tauern National Park rising dramatically to the south. Utilized by traders as far back as the Bronze and Roman ages for transporting copper and alpine salt, the pass plateau today is an idyllic sanctuary famed for primeval raised peat bogs, aromatic Swiss stone pine woodlands, and tranquil high pastures overlooking the majestic Grossvenediger massif.

Route & Anforderungen

The Pass Thurn highway (B161) remains open year-round, featuring a well-engineered asphalt surface with moderate gradients rarely exceeding eight percent, making it comfortable for caravans, motorhomes, and recreational cyclists. From Kitzbühel, the road winds gently past Aurach and Jochberg through fragrant mountain forests. At the crest of the pass, visitors will find diverse hiking routes ranging from leisurely nature walks to full-day ridge climbs. A primary highlight is the Wasenmoos Nature Trail, a barrier-free boardwalk path looping through an internationally recognized wetland ecosystem that is ideally suited for families. Ambitious hikers can ascend toward the Resterkogel (1,894 m) along well-graded alpine footpaths demanding standard hiking shoes and weather protection.

Besuch & Anreise

Approaching from Innsbruck or Munich, motorists follow motorway A12 to Wörgl or Kufstein, continuing along the B170 and B161 through Kitzbühel and Jochberg to the pass summit. From the south, federal road B161 connects directly from Mittersill in the Salzach valley. Regular regional public bus routes connect Kitzbühel and Mittersill, stopping directly at the pass summit. Plentiful free parking is available at the pass crest and near the Wasenmoos trailhead.

Tipps

Take an evening stroll along the wooden boardwalks of the Wasenmoos bog when blooming cotton grass covers the landscape in white tufts. The adjacent Kitzbühel Alps Panorama Cable Car offers swift access to high-altitude ridge paths and traditional alpine huts serving homemade Austrian delicacies.
